QUOTE: "`allow` is consulted in `check_approval` through `is_explicitly_allowed`. A match skips the approval prompt. It does not override the deny list, because `execute` checks deny afterward."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the allow list only skips the approval prompt in `ToolExecutor::check_approval`. It also says allow does not grant execution, because `ServerManager::execute` still applies the deny list separately.
